name: ReSearch: Learning to Reason with Search for LLMs via Reinforcement Learning
venue: NeurIPS 2025 (preprint arXiv:2503.19470, v1 Mar 2025, v3 Sep 2025; cs.AI / cs.CL)
authors_affiliation: Mingyang Chen, Tianpeng Li, Haoze Sun, Yijie Zhou, Chenzheng Zhu, Fan Yang, Zenan Zhou, Weipeng Chen (Baichuan Inc.); Linzhuang Sun (University of Chinese Academy of Sciences); Haofen Wang (Tongji University); Jeff Z. Pan (University of Edinburgh); Wen Zhang, Huajun Chen (Zhejiang University). Lead/corresponding: Mingyang Chen, Fan Yang (Baichuan Inc.).
code_url: https://github.com/Agent-RL/ReSearch (original implementation archived in the 're-search' branch of the repo, which has since been renamed/superseded by https://github.com/Agent-RL/ReCall; trained models at https://huggingface.co/collections/agentrl/research-67e506a0311bea06dc54878b)
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/Agent-RL/ReCall (successor framework ReCall extends ReSearch to general tool-use; ReSearch code archived in 're-search' branch; ~1.4k stars, MIT license)
task_domain: QA (multi-hop / knowledge-intensive question answering requiring multi-step reasoning interleaved with search); search-augmented reasoning.
problem_setting: Interactive single-agent multi-step RAG: an LLM policy is trained from scratch via reinforcement learning (GRPO) to reason and decide when/how to issue search queries against an external Wikipedia retrieval environment, with retrieval results fed back into the ongoing reasoning chain. No supervised data on reasoning steps or search trajectories is used; only question-answer pairs with a rule-based outcome reward. Training uses a single dataset (MuSiQue train set); evaluation is zero-shot/out-of-domain on additional multi-hop QA benchmarks.
what_is_retrieved: Documents/passages (Wikipedia background knowledge passages retrieved by a dense retriever in response to model-generated search queries).
retrieval_grounding: STATIC external corpus (Wikipedia Dec. 2018 dump indexed by FlashRAG; no agent-written growing memory).
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Fixed top-k ranking per query (top-5 passages returned per search call); no explicit completeness/minimal-set or precision-driven variable-size objective. The model can issue multiple search calls iteratively, so overall coverage emerges from repeated top-k retrievals rather than a single completeness target.
explicit_cbr_grounding: False; the work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner.
retrieval_unit: document/passage (Wikipedia text passages; top-5 per query enclosed in <result></result> tags).
index_source: Static offline-built corpus: pre-indexed Wikipedia (Dec. 2018) via FlashRAG; embeddings/index preprocessed offline; the retrievable store is frozen and does not grow during training or test time.
index_structure_topology: Flat dense vector index (E5-base-v2 embeddings over Wikipedia passages, FlashRAG/FAISS); no graph or hierarchical organization.
retriever_type: Dense (E5-base-v2 dense retriever, off-the-shelf); a BM25/keyword option is not the primary configuration.
retriever_learning_signal: None for the retriever itself (off-the-shelf E5-base-v2, frozen). The learned component is the LLM policy that decides when and how (query formulation) to retrieve; the policy is trained by RL (GRPO) on a final-outcome reward (F1-based answer reward + format reward). The retriever is not trained.
query_construction: Thought-conditioned: the policy LLM generates a natural-language search query inside <search></search> tags during its <think> reasoning; queries are produced free-form by the model as a function of the question and prior retrieval results (supports query refinement / self-correction of queries).
query_granularity: Step/state-level: queries are emitted at each reasoning step where the model decides to search (multiple search queries per rollout), rather than one-shot at t=0.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative and agent-initiated/adaptive: the model decides at each step whether to emit a <search>; the rollout alternates think -> search -> result -> think until an <answer> / eos. When-and-how-to-search is learned, not on a fixed schedule.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Agent-initiated request: retrieval is triggered when the generation produces a </search> tag (the policy emits a search query as part of its text-based thinking). The decision to search is learned through RL rather than from a confidence threshold, learned complexity classifier, or reflection tokens.
reranking: None reported; the dense retriever's top-5 passages are returned directly without a separate reranking stage.
retrieved_context_refinement: None / minimal: retrieved top-5 passages are inserted verbatim into the reasoning context (enclosed in <result></result>); no decompose-recompose, distillation, distractor filtering, or compression. The only special handling is loss masking of retrieved tokens during training.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (search is a single fixed tool; no per-tool description engineering). Tool invocation is conveyed via a simple prompt template instructing use of the wikipedia search tool with <search></search> tags.
index_content_separation: N/A (no progressive-disclosure index vs content separation; flat dense index).
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A for ReSearch (static Wikipedia index; search exposed via a FlashRAG/FastAPI retriever service). The successor ReCall generalizes to arbitrary user-defined tools, but ReSearch itself uses a single static search tool.
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (single search tool; no inter-tool dependency modeling).
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation as part of an RL training signal: retrieved results are concatenated back into the rollout as context for further reasoning; the whole reason-with-search rollout is optimized via GRPO toward a final-answer reward (retrieved tokens are masked out of the policy-gradient loss so the policy is not trained to imitate retrieved text).
planning_integration: Inside a search loop / per-step interleaved: search is woven into the reasoning chain itself (think -> search -> result -> think -> ... -> answer). There is no separate planner module; the reasoning chain is the plan and retrieval is an integral component of it.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-reasoning-step / per-search-call within a rollout: each <think> step may issue one <search> call, and retrieval results condition subsequent reasoning; interleaving is at the level of individual thinking steps rather than per-token or per-final-answer.
retrieved_item_representation: Raw retrieved passages (top-5 Wikipedia text snippets) injected verbatim inside <result></result> tags; no distillation into strategy/guideline/program form.
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: Raw document/passage (concrete retrieved Wikipedia text), not a distilled strategy, workflow, or skill.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Retriever-aware / RL training: the policy is trained end-to-end with GRPO so it learns to reason over (and self-correct against) imperfect retrieval; retrieved-result tokens are masked in the loss to prevent the policy from being biased toward retrieved text. Reflection/self-correction (e.g., recognizing a failed query and reformulating) emerges naturally from RL rather than from an explicit relevance evaluator.
memory_type: none (no episodic store, skill library, or persistent memory; retrieval is against a static external corpus).
write_back: False; the system does not store new experiences/cases/skills into any memory. Learning is captured in the policy LLM's weights via RL, not in a retrievable store.
online_growth: False; the retrievable Wikipedia store is frozen (built offline) and does not grow during deployment or test time.
write_back_trigger: never (no write-back to a retrievable memory; the only updating is offline RL policy-weight updates from final-outcome rewards).
failure_experience_usage: No explicit storage/retrieval of failed experiences. During RL, low-reward rollouts (including format-incorrect or wrong-answer ones) receive lower normalized advantage in GRPO (reward 0 / 0.1 / F1), implicitly discouraging failure patterns, but failures are not stored as retrievable cases. Reflection/self-correction within a rollout is an emergent behavior, not a stored failure rule.
memory_evolution_update: N/A (no stored memory entries to mutate).
retrieval_as_learned_policy: Yes (partially): the decision of WHEN to retrieve and HOW to formulate the query is a learned RL policy (GRPO-optimized LLM) rather than a fixed similarity top-k schedule. The underlying passage ranking for a given query remains a fixed off-the-shelf dense top-k retriever.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No; single-agent, single-policy. No cross-agent or cross-framework memory/experience sharing.
benchmarks: HotpotQA (full dev, 7405), 2WikiMultiHopQA (full dev, 12576), MuSiQue (full dev, 2417; also the sole training source, train set 19938 samples), Bamboogle (test, 125). Retrieval environment: Wikipedia (Dec. 2018) via FlashRAG with E5-base-v2, top-5.
benchmark_family: Multi-hop QA (open-domain multi-hop question answering over Wikipedia).
baselines: No RAG / Naive Generation (instruction-tuned model answers directly), Naive RAG (concatenate retrieved passages with question then answer), Iter-RetGen (iterative retrieve-generate synergy), IRCoT (interleaved retrieval with chain-of-thought). Prompt-based baselines use instruction-tuned Qwen2.5 models of the same size for fair comparison. Backbones: Qwen2.5-7B, Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, Qwen2.5-32B, Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct.
key_metrics: Exact Match (EM, %) and LLM-as-a-Judge (LJ, %, using gpt-4o-mini as judge). Training/analysis metrics: training & validation reward, response length, average number of search operations per rollout.
headline_result: ReSearch outperforms all baselines on all four multi-hop QA benchmarks. Average improvement over the best baseline: +15.81% EM / +17.56% LJ for 7B models and +14.82% EM / +15.46% LJ for 32B models (absolute improvements over baselines range 8.9%-22.4%). Best single configuration (ReSearch-Qwen-32B-Instruct): e.g., Bamboogle 56.80 EM / 67.20 LJ; HotpotQA 46.73 EM / 67.70 LJ; MuSiQue 26.40 EM / 38.56 LJ; 2Wiki 44.90 EM / 50.30 LJ.
ablations: No standard component-ablation table; the paper instead provides comparative analyses: (1) base vs instruction-tuned starting models (instruction-tuned consistently better across all benchmarks/sizes; both trained by RL from scratch with no SFT); (2) 7B vs 32B scale; (3) training-dynamics analyses showing response length and average number of search operations both grow over training (model learns to search more / rely less on internal knowledge, especially 32B); (4) training vs validation reward curves (sharp rise in first ~20 steps); (5) generalization analysis (trained only on MuSiQue, generalizes to HotpotQA/2Wiki/Bamboogle); (6) case study showing emergent reflection/self-correction ('I made a mistake' -> reformulated query). Retrieval-result loss masking is a design choice motivated but not separately ablated [uncertain whether masking was quantitatively ablated].
evaluation_decoupling: No; only end-to-end task metrics (EM, LJ) are reported. No intrinsic retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG / completeness) are reported separately.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Primarily outcome-based (final-answer EM and LLM-as-a-Judge). Process is examined qualitatively/diagnostically (number of search operations, response length, reward curves, and a case study of reflection/self-correction) but not scored as a quantitative process-quality metric.
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: Response length (tokens excluding retrieval results) is reported as a proxy for test-time reasoning cost and grows during training; the average number of search operations per rollout also grows during training (more retrieval calls = more cost but higher accuracy). Top-5 passages retrieved per query. Training cost: 8x8 (=64) NVIDIA H800 GPUs, full-parameter optimization with gradient checkpointing, 2 training epochs on MuSiQue (19938 samples). No explicit latency/API-cost-vs-accuracy frontier table is given.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Fixed-k retrieval: top-5 passages per search query. Multiple search calls allowed per rollout, so total injected context grows with the number of searches. Inference context length 8192 (per ReCall serving config). No adaptive/precision-driven k or explicit token-budget cap on injected items is reported beyond fixed top-5.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (not a benchmark paper; uses existing datasets). Evaluation sizes: HotpotQA dev 7405, 2WikiMultiHopQA dev 12576, MuSiQue dev 2417, Bamboogle test 125; original context documents discarded so only Q-A pairs are used with an open-ended Wikipedia retrieval environment.
builds_on: DeepSeek-R1 / OpenAI-o1-style RL-for-reasoning (rule-based reward, RL without supervised reasoning steps); GRPO (DeepSeekMath / Group Relative Policy Optimization) as the RL algorithm; verl RL framework; FlashRAG retrieval toolkit with E5-base-v2 retriever; Qwen2.5 (7B/32B, base and instruct) backbones.
contrasts_with: Prompt/heuristic-based multi-step RAG methods (Iter-RetGen, IRCoT) and naive RAG / no-RAG baselines; self-reflection RAG such as Self-RAG; SFT-based imitation of reasoning-with-search trajectories (ReSearch uses no supervised reasoning/search data). Concurrent RL-search work (e.g., Search-R1) is in the same line; ReSearch emphasizes treating search as an integral part of the reasoning chain trained purely via outcome RL.
lineage: Part of the B (RAG / task-solving) lineage of RL-trained reason-with-search / agentic-RAG methods (alongside Search-R1): LLM policy learns interleaved reasoning + retrieval from outcome rewards over a static corpus, rather than relying on prompting heuristics or growing experiential memory. Direct predecessor in spirit to the authors' own successor framework ReCall, which generalizes search to arbitrary tool calls.
